newsitem.title: CHINA: China cuts rice liquor output to save grain.
newsitem.headline: China cuts rice liquor output to save grain.

text.p: China is cutting production of rice liquors and making more fruit wine and beer as part of a plan to reduce grain consumption, the official Xinhua news agency said on Sunday.
"The industry has to solve the problem of huge grain consumption to ensure healthy development in the future," said Wang Lizeng, a division chief with the China National Council of Light Industry.
Rice liquor distilleries are a major consumer of grain.
About 14 million tonnes of grain are used each year to make white spirits, Wang said. Output of white spirits is expected to total 7.0 million tonnes this year.

The amount of grain used to make white spirits is enough to feed about 30 million people for a year, Xinhua said, adding that such usage was unsuitable for a country that must feed 1.2 billion people.
China must limit white spirit output and reduce the alcohol content to save grain, Wang said. Xinhua gave no more details.
